title: From November 1, RIMS campus closed as a shortcut
summary: The hospital cites safety concerns, including an alleged attack on a dental student, after incidents on its premises.
body:
From November 1, the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Imphal will stop people from using its campus as a bypass or through-route.

The institute's notice points to an alleged attempt on the life of a BDS student, frequent thefts of institute property, and people using open areas of the campus to take intoxicants.

Access will be limited to patients, their attendants, doctors, staff and others with real business at RIMS. Staff have been asked to carry ID cards and show vehicle passes when asked.

The new rule follows an attack reported earlier in October. In a press release dated October 2, RIMS said a female BDS student was jogging inside the campus at about 5.30 pm when a person whose face was hidden by a mask and a hoodie came up to her and tried to hit her with a hammer. She dodged the blow and was not seriously hurt. The student and the institute both filed FIRs with the police.

As an immediate step at that time, RIMS barred outsiders from entering the campus after 5 pm for jogging, recreation or other non-essential reasons, and asked staff to carry and display their ID cards. The November 1 rule goes further by ending the use of the campus as a through-route altogether.

The RIMS authority said the new measure is meant to tighten security, control vehicle movement and protect students, patients, staff and the institute's property. It asked the public to cooperate and to stop using the campus as a shortcut.

RIMS is located at Lamphelpat on the edge of Imphal and its campus covers about 192 acres. It began as a regional medical college in 1972 and has been run by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare since April 2007. Its teaching hospital has 1,074 beds, and the institute serves as a regional centre for medical education in the Northeast.
